decision: The secret stack (deploy/aws/templates/50-secret.yaml) creates one secret, proposal-orchestrator/env-config, retained on deletion and replacement, encrypted with the imported KeyArn, with no rotation and no replica, tagged project only, whose value is one JSON object of five non-credential keys built in the template (ORCHESTRATOR_TRANSPORT_PRESET = BEDROCK_CONVERSE_EU, ORCHESTRATOR_PRODUCTION_MODE = true, ORCHESTRATOR_DIAGNOSTIC_LEVEL = metadata, AWS_REGION from AWS::Region, ORCHESTRATOR_TRANSPORT_MODEL from TransportModelId); and one deny-only resource policy with BlockPublicPolicy: the runtime role may do nothing but GetSecretValue, only the runtime role and the admin role read the value, only the admin role changes, deletes, restores, tags, rotates or replicates the secret, and no principal outside the account acts on it. No deny touches the policy-management actions or DescribeSecret for a principal of the account other than the runtime role, and the admin exception matches the role ARN with and without its /managed/ path. It exports SecretArn and SecretName.
why: Ticket R8 and its exit conditions; OD8 (a) makes the secret the host's configuration source (F4). Same-account access already comes from IAM (R5 identity policy and boundary for the runtime role, AdministratorAccess for the admin role), so the resource policy only narrows, as R7-D3 did for the deploy bucket. The account has no root user (F-OD11r2-3), so the lockout guard is built into the policy itself.

AWS::SecretsManager::Secret: omitting both value properties creates an empty secret; a change of the value property creates a new version; KmsKeyId takes an ARN, key id or alias and defaults to aws/secretsmanager; only Name requires replacement; Ref and GetAtt Id return the ARN; the page says nothing about stack-deletion behaviour or drift on the value. decisions.answer: Proceed. The secret costs 0.40 USD per month, prorated, plus 0.05 USD per 10,000 API requests in eu-north-1 (F-R8-2), paid from credits: the 'free (secret: monthly)' case of OD6-r3, not an hourly-billed resource of the kind R11 gates.

decisions.question: How the values enter the secret (point 2)
decisions.answer: (a) In the template: the value property is a single-string Fn::Sub of a JSON object of exactly five keys, built from TransportModelId and AWS::Region. The values change only by an UPDATE of this template, never by put-secret-value. Evidence uses describe-change-set without --include-property-values.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '2a'. The values are configuration already in the parameter file, not credentials; reproducible and reviewed in the change set.
decisions.consequence: The five values are visible in get-template and the CloudFormation console. R12b reads them on the host through the R9 launcher.

decisions.question: The preset value (point 3)
decisions.answer: (a) ORCHESTRATOR_TRANSPORT_PRESET = BEDROCK_CONVERSE_EU, a lasting rule: R9e implements a preset of exactly this name (backend bedrock_converse, default Region eu-north-1, eu. profiles), with a test that the name stored by 50-secret.yaml exists in runner/transport/config.py.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '3a'. DC-34 speaks of a preset; R11 does not need the launcher.
decisions.consequence: Until R9e lands, a launcher reading the secret fails closed on the unknown preset (get_transport_preset raises). plans/aws_redeployment_tickets.md R9e records the rule.

decisions.question: Resource policy (point 4)
decisions.answer: (b) Deny-only, BlockPublicPolicy true, no Allow statement; its statements are R8-D12 and R8-D13.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '4a' (the proposal). A same-account Allow would duplicate R5's identity grant (as in R7-D3).
decisions.consequence: The admin role keeps full access through IAM except where R8-D13 narrows it; any AWS service needing the secret from another account is refused.

decisions.question: Retention and deletion (point 5)
decisions.answer: DeletionPolicy Retain and UpdateReplacePolicy Retain on the secret; the resource policy goes with the stack; the secret stack is not deleted.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '5a'. The host depends on the secret, and a secret in its recovery window is expected to hold its name (F-R8-6 known gap).
decisions.consequence: Deleting the stack would leave the secret without its policy; a recreated stack would collide on the name.

decisions.question: Rotation and replicas (point 6)
decisions.answer: None: no RotationSchedule resource, no ReplicaRegions property.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '6a'. No credential to rotate (R8-D14); EU single-Region.

decisions.question: How 'key names and metadata only' is evidenced (point 7)

No get-secret-value command appears in STEPS.md.
decisions.consequence: The read also shows that the admin exception of R8-D12 matches (an explicit deny would refuse it).

decisions.question: Admin lockout (point 12, added by the agent)
decisions.answer: (c) No deny touches GetResourcePolicy, PutResourcePolicy, DeleteResourcePolicy or DescribeSecret for a principal of the account other than the runtime role; and the admin exception lists the role ARN with its path (AdminRoleArn) and without it (built with Fn::Select [2, Fn::Split ['/', AdminRoleArn]]), under ArnNotLike.
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '12a' (= (c)). No root user exists (F-OD11r2-3); whether aws:PrincipalArn carries the path is not documented (F-R8-4).
decisions.consequence: Even if neither form matched, the admin role could still replace or delete the policy. Round 2 shows which form matches by the admin's value read (R8-D7). AdminRoleArn must keep exactly one path segment; the test checks it.

decisions.question: Deny scope (point 13, added by the agent)
decisions.answer: (b) Four statements: DenyRuntimeRoleExceptGetSecretValue (NotAction GetSecretValue, ArnEquals the runtime role); DenyValueReadExceptRuntimeAndAdmin (GetSecretValue, ArnNotLike runtime role and both admin forms); DenyChangesExceptAdmin (PutSecretValue, UpdateSecret, UpdateSecretVersionStage, DeleteSecret, RestoreSecret, RotateSecret, CancelRotateSecret, TagResource, UntagResource, ReplicateSecretToRegions, RemoveRegionsFromReplication, StopReplicationToReplica; ArnNotLike both admin forms); DenyPrincipalsOutsideAccount (secretsmanager:*, StringNotEquals aws:PrincipalAccount).
decisions.reason: Operator's answer '13a' (= (b)). A service-linked role of the account may still read metadata, never the value.
decisions.consequence: CloudFormation acts with the admin role's credentials (no service role), so stack updates fall under the admin exception. BatchGetSecretValue also needs GetSecretValue per secret and is therefore covered.

known_gaps.gap: That a secret scheduled for deletion holds its name through the recovery window, and what CloudFormation does with a deleted Secret resource (F-R8-5, F-R8-6). Moot while Retain holds and the stack is not deleted.
Which admin ARN form aws:PrincipalArn carries (F-R8-4). Round 2's admin read (R8_09_key-names-digest.txt, not denied) shows that one of the two forms matches; it cannot show which.
Whether CloudFormation drift detection covers the value property (F-R8-5); the rule 'template UPDATE only' stands in for it.
BEDROCK_CONVERSE_EU does not exist until R9e; until then the stored preset is not resolvable by runner/transport/config.py.

The AWS-managed organization's RCPs can apply to Secrets Manager and KMS and are not visible from the member account (OD11-r2 known gap); a restriction shows as an explicit deny at the change set or at creation.
That the runtime role reads the secret through Secrets Manager's use of the key (R6-D3) is shown only by R11's live call from the host.
